title: etbb-july-2024-february-2026-update.pdf — section 472
text:
46. These practices should be accommodated where possible, to enable such witnesses to
consider themselves most conscience-bound to tell the truth.
Asking people how they would like to take the oath

47. Court and tribunal staff should present witnesses and jurors with a choice of two equally
valid procedures before they come into court: making an affirmation or swearing an oath.

48. Witnesses do not always understand the meaning of the word “affirm”. This should be
explained rather than waiting for the individual to ask.

49. It is important to do this before the witness/juror comes into the courtroom so that there is
time to locate the appropriate religious book.

50. If they wish to swear an oath, witnesses should be informed about the availability of different
holy books in court and invited to identify the holy book on which they wish to swear the
oath.
